senses.en_definition: To drive or operate a vehicle, aircraft, or other means of transport.
To lead or guide someone or direct their thinking.
To try out or test something; to try on clothing.

messages.en: Have you set off yet? I'm waiting in the lobby.
Just got in the car. I'm about to start driving, so I'll message you when I get there.
Okay, no need to reply for now. I'll just wait.

senses.en_definition: Indeed; really; used to confirm a fact or emphasise a judgement.
Naturally; as is right or to be expected.

messages.en: Have you tried the nasi lemak at that place I told you about?
I have! It's really good, and the sambal's great too. I reckon I'll go again tomorrow.

senses.en_definition: To call someone to come or return, usually by calling out their name.
To summon or invite someone to come or attend.
To address or refer to someone by a particular name, title, or nickname.

messages.en: Can I just call you Aina? Or should I call you Ms Aina?
Just call me Aina, no need to be so formal. I'll call you Farhan too, okay?
Sure, that keeps things simple. See you at the office later!

collocations.en: call out loudly to him or her

messages.en: Is Amir still in the canteen? The teacher called him earlier, but he didn't hear a thing.
Yeah, he's still there. I'll go and tell him now.
